requirement: A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test sources alone. I did not request implementation source. The tests adequately check every obligation in `requirements.ci.fence_lengths`.

**Obligations derived from the text**
1. A `{req}` opening fence of four or more colons is accepted. Any length of at least three works.
2. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener stays inside the body, so a nested colon directive is allowed.
3. A closing fence outside a fenced code example, with at least as many colons as the opener, ends the body. This covers a closer that is equal in length or longer.

**Mapping to tests**
- **Obligations 1 and 3 (accepted lengths, closer lengths).** `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers]` runs `validate_repository` with three opener/closer pairs: `::::`/`::::`, `::::`/`:::::`, and `:::::::`/`::::::::`.
  - These cover equal closers and longer closers, at several opener lengths.
  - The evidence JSON must match the full body. If the body ended early at the nested `:::`, or ran past the closer, validation would report an error. The test asserts that the requirement count is 1 and that there are no errors.
- **Obligation 2 (shorter colon line stays inside).** The same test nests `:::{note} … :::` inside a 4+-colon opener and expects the text after it ("Still in the requirement.") to remain in the body. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]` asserts directly on `definition_blocks`. It checks that there is one block, that it is closed, that its body is exactly `Intro.\n\n:::{note}\nNested.\n:::\n`, and that "Outside." falls after the end.
- **Obligation 3, three-colon default and code-example exclusion.** `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text]` puts a `:::` line inside a ```text code fence in a three-colon requirement. The requirement text must include that line and the markdown that follows it, and must exclude the text after the real closer. `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code]` checks several cases.
  - A `:::::` closer closes a `:::` opener.
  - Inside a `::::` fence, a nested `:::` closer does not close the outer fence.
  - A `:::` line inside a code fence is skipped when the code-aware mode is on, and counted when it is off.
  - A fence that never closes is reported as unclosed.
- **Examples.** `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace]` covers `{example}` fences with 4 and 6 colons, longer closers, nested `:::{note}`, and a literal `:::{example}` inside a code fence. This is extra coverage, since the requirement text names `{req}`.

**Gaps**
I found no gaps and no marking gaps. Each test carries a `{test}` reference to the requirement. The tests assert on body extents and validation outcomes, not only on execution. The requirement's wording leaves no ambiguity that would change a conclusion.
